maria: Quick experiment update — I flipped the "drift-aware" batch allocator to staging for ~2h on the mixed long+short traffic profile. Wanted to surface numbers and get ideas for preventing long-tenant regressions. TL;DR: short-seq latency improved, long-seq tail regressed. Logs & configs below.

kai: Can you paste p50/p95/p99 and a per-tenant split? Also any KV-hit changes? :thinking:

maria: Sure — extracting the key metrics from the perf dump. Baseline vs drift-aware experiment (10m windows aggregated):
- short-tenant (median seq len 40): p50 12ms -> 9ms (-25%), p95 48ms -> 30ms (-37%), p99 210ms -> 160ms (-24%)
- long-tenant (median seq len 1200): p50 420ms -> 430ms (+2%), p95 1200ms -> 1700ms (+42%), p99 4200ms -> 6800ms (+62%)
KV cache hit-rate overall: 72% -> 80% (improved prefix reuse for shorts). CPU utilization +15% on the GPU host due to smaller, more frequent kernels.

ashok: That pattern smells like batch formation preference for many short requests — allocator groups many small tokens into fast mini-batches and consumes token-budget credits, starving long sequences that need large continuous tokens. The drift-aware heuristic lowers batch formation latency for shorts by decaying grouping thresholds, but we didn't reserve tail credits for long sequences.

jin: Proposed config tweak to test soft reservations and age-preemption (pseudo-config):
```
batch_allocator:
  mode: drift-aware
  drift_decay_ms: 400
  token_budget_target: 0.65
  soft_reserve_tokens_per_long_tenant: 2000
  age_preempt_ms: 150
  long_seq_threshold_tokens: 512
```
The idea: keep most of the short-path gains but ensure long tenants get a small guaranteed slice of token credits and that very old queued long heads can preempt.

maria: This looks promising. A few follow-ups: (1) how do we detect "long tenant" without adding heavy classification? (2) will soft_reserve interact badly with autoscaling/burst pools?

kai: For (1) we can do a cheap heuristic: if request.max_output_tokens + input_len > long_seq_threshold_tokens then mark as long for the bucket. That avoids per-tenant metadata. For (2) soft_reserve should be accounted as a low-priority reservation that doesn't block autoscale, but it must decrement same token budget counters so we don't overcommit. We should also try kernel hinting: group requests by estimated output token length right before kernel-selection so longs get scheduled to slower-path kernels in fewer, denser micro-batches.

devbot: perf/regression-checker: run #2389 completed. Findings: long-seq p99 regression +62% relative on drift-aware. Short-seq aggregate improved p95 by 37%. Flagging as regression for long-tenant SLA.

ashok: Another simple scheduling tweak: add age-based preemption with token-aware condition. Pseudo-sched: 
```
for head in queue:
  if head.age_ms > age_preempt_ms and head.estimated_tokens > soft_reserve_threshold:
    mark_for_early_dispatch(head)
```
This avoids forcefully draining the global token reservoir but prevents indefinite delay of long heads. Also consider fractional crediting: instead of single global token_budget, keep two buckets (short_bucket, long_bucket) with periodic rebalancing to adapt to workload drift.

maria: I like the two-bucket + age-preempt approach. Plan: create a canary variant (5%) that enables soft_reserve + age_preempt + kernel grouping by length. Metrics to watch: per-tenant p99, KV hit-rate, throughput (tokens/sec), and GPU kernel-switch churn. Rollout steps: canary -> 25% -> 100% if long p99 doesn't regress >10% and short p95 gains are preserved.

kai: I'll run a focused microbench with a 70/30 short/long mix and the proposed config. Command: `bench/run --scenario long+short-mix --duration 10m --variant drift-soft-reserve --trace` I'll post traces to the perf bucket. :thumbsup:

jin: Small instrumentation requests before canary: emit token-bucket levels per-lane every 5s, and a histogram of queue head ages by estimated_token_size. That should make debugging easier if we see intermittent starvation.

maria: Agreed. I'll wire up the logs and the canary YAML. Thanks y'all — will post results in this thread when bench completes.
